content: 4-Desoxymescaline, also known as 4-methyl-3,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine, is a chemical compound classified as a phenethylamine and an analogue of mescaline. It exhibits psychedelic properties and is commonly referred to by the shorthand name DESOXY. This compound was first synthesized and documented by Alexander Shulgin, with its details published in the book PiHKAL (Phenethylamines I Have Known and Loved). In the United States, mescaline was classified as a Schedule I controlled substance under the Controlled Substances Act of 1970. Similarly, mescaline and its analogues are regulated in many other countries. Under the Federal Analogue Act, 4-desoxymescaline could be considered an analogue of mescaline, which would render its manufacture, purchase, possession, or distribution illegal without proper authorization from the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). The typical dosage range for 4-desoxymescaline is reported to be between 40 and 120 milligrams, with effects lasting approximately 6 to 8 hours. Despite its structural similarity to mescaline, the effects of 4-desoxymescaline are reported to differ significantly. Users have described experiencing an elevated mood and mild hallucinations, though these visual effects are notably less intense than those associated with mescaline. There is speculation that the standard dosage range of 40 to 120 milligrams may be insufficient to produce effects comparable to mescaline. However, due to the limited number of human studies conducted with this compound, increasing the dosage could pose significant safety risks.
